description: A spear-thrower is a short board or shaft with a hook that engages the butt of a light spear, or dart, lengthening the arm's lever so the dart flies farther. Carved examples survive from Upper Palaeolithic France, roughly 20,000 to 15,000 years ago. Aboriginal Australians and peoples of the Americas also used it; Aztec warriors still did.
uncertainty: The proposal dates emergence to about 30,000 years ago in Europe; the oldest surviving examples are younger, and earlier use is inferred from projectile points and debated. Australian and American traditions are generally treated as separate developments.
